item.title: Lancang-Mekong cooperation stressed
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Lancang-Mekong countries agreed on Wednesday to deepen security cooperation and intensify joint efforts against cross-border crime to safeguard regional peace, as they work to build a Lancang-Mekong community with a shared future. The commitments came at the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Beijing, which was cochaired by Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow. Senior officials from Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and Myanmar also attended the meeting. Wang called for stepping up joint efforts to combat cross-border crime, including online gambling, telecom fraud, drug trafficking, counterfeiting and smuggling, and ensuring the continued success of the Safe Lancang-Mekong Operation and the joint patrol of the Mekong River. The countries should firmly oppose external interference and attempts to provoke bloc confrontation, resist exclusive groupings and never allow a revival of militarism, he said. Noting that this year marks the 10th anniversary of the mechanism's first leaders' meeting, Wang said that Lancang-Mekong Cooperation has become a golden example of regional cooperation. He attributed its growth to the six countries' commitment to good-neighborliness and a shared future, their focus on development and practical cooperation, dedication to benefiting people and upholding openness and inclusiveness, and courage to pursue innovation and pioneer new approaches. According to Chinese figures, trade between China and the five Mekong countries exceeded $500 billion in 2025, up 150 percent from a decade ago, accounting for about half of China's total trade with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. The Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Special Fund has supported more than 1,000 development projects across the region. Wang also called for closer exchanges and policy coordination, as well as the greater sharing of governance experience. Differences and disputes should be resolved through dialogue and consultation, while development cooperation should help strengthen security resilience, he added. He urged the countries to better align their development strategies, deepen cooperation on the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, and promote regional trade and investment liberalization and facilitation. Wang called for stronger joint research, technical cooperation and personnel training, the establishment of a Lancang-Mekong poverty reduction cooperation center and more "small and beautiful" livelihood projects. He advocated closer cooperation in emerging fields, including the digital economy, artificial intelligence, smart manufacturing and smart agriculture, adding that China welcomes more Mekong countries to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. To improve disaster preparedness, Wang proposed establishing a cross-border disaster early-warning cooperation mechanism and a mechanism for the real-time exchange of hydrological, meteorological, geological and forest fire data. Senior officials from the five Mekong countries commended China's leading role in advancing cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to promoting the region's sustainable development and prosperity. They pledged to strengthen coordination between Lancang-Mekong Cooperation and other regional mechanisms, uphold multilateralism and jointly address global challenges. All sides agreed to maintain close communication to ensure the success of the fifth Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Leaders' Meeting. The ministerial meeting adopted the 2025 progress report on implementing the Five-Year Plan of Action on Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (2023-27) and the 2026 list of projects supported by the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Special Fund. Du Lan, deputy director of the Department for Asia-Pacific Studies at the China Institute of International Studies, said that Lancang-Mekong Cooperation has demonstrated how developing countries can achieve shared development through cooperation on an equal footing.

item.title: Why the CPC has always been committed to advancing self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
The fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, held in Beijing from Oct 26 to 29, focused on a pivotal issue for the country's future: the Party's capacity to govern itself while steering a highly complex modernization process. The meeting examined measures to promote the implementation of full and rigorous Party self-governance at a time when China is embarking on the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period, a crucial phase aimed at basically achieving socialist modernization by 2035. This is not just about strengthening internal discipline, combating corruption or ensuring compliance with directives. It is about preserving the political, organizational and moral capacity of a force that is the decisive agent of China's modernization. As development demands grow, so too must the Party's ability to anticipate challenges, address shortcomings and maintain its connection with society. The emphasis on full and rigorous Party self-governance highlights the challenges ahead. China must sustain its economic and technological transformation, address structural imbalances and meet social expectations amid an increasingly uncertain and competitive international environment. The CPC realizes that these challenges cannot be met through economic policies, administrative reforms or technological investment alone. They also require an organization capable of implementing decisions, coordinating different levels of government and maintaining strategic consistency. Therefore, raising the standards of conduct and performance, addressing persistent problems and strengthening oversight mechanisms are necessary. Keeping the Party in good working order is a continuous requirement for effective governance. This approach is an extension of the CPC's long-standing concern about how to prevent a revolutionary organization, once transformed into a ruling party, from losing the vitality, discipline and social connectedness that fueled its rise. Full and rigorous self-governance is aimed at identifying and tackling internal contradictions before they undermine its legitimacy and effectiveness. This approach carries broader and longer-term political significance by strengthening the capacity for self-correction, thereby helping to sustain trust and institutional legitimacy. Governing for an extended period is not enough; the Party must develop the capabilities required to do so without allowing the prolonged exercise of power to weaken the very organization that wields it. The trajectory of self-governance has expanded in scope. The eight-point decision of December 2012 established standards of conduct for leading cadres. What began as an intervention targeting specific behaviors has evolved into a broader strategy of organizational transformation. The difference lies not only in the intensity of the measures, but also in their implementation. The fight against corruption is increasingly integrated with oversight systems, disciplinary inspections, internal regulations and the supervision of power. The goal is to simultaneously move in three directions: ensuring that officials are unable to engage in corruption, dare not do so, and have no desire to do so. This formula combines institutional prevention, sanctions and political education. This evolution points to a significant innovation in governance that turns oversight into a systematic and permanent function. The CPC aims to prevent public policies from deviating from their objectives. The challenge is to combine discipline, accountability and initiative, while avoiding a situation where the fear of making mistakes leads to inaction. Strict self-governance aims to preserve the Party's nature and founding mission. The concept rests on the premise that an organization aspiring to exercise power over the long term must develop mechanisms for detecting and correcting deviations. Renewal cannot depend solely on external pressures or exceptional interventions; it must become an integral part of the Party's regular functioning. The legitimacy of this endeavor also depends on the Party's relationship with society. It must demonstrate that its priorities translate into tangible improvements in people's lives. One of the most demanding challenges of contemporary governance is ensuring that political commitments align with social reality. This challenge is not unique to China; no political party in any country can indefinitely take its public connection for granted. The fifth plenary session is significant in light of the stage of China's modernization. As tasks grow more complex, the quality of Party cadres becomes increasingly important. Grand strategies succeed only if those responsible for implementing them, from the central leadership to local levels, understand their objectives and can adapt them to specific circumstances. Compliance with directives is necessary, but not sufficient. Professional competence, initiative, social awareness and willingness to assume responsibility also matter. The question is how to instill a commitment to modernization throughout the Party's structure, fostering conviction, creativity and a sense of public service. For discipline to translate into governing capacity, it must be supported by training, evaluation, clear responsibilities and recognition of achievements. The fifth plenary session reflects the Chinese leadership's belief that the success of modernization largely depends on the Party's ability to renew itself and maintain cohesion, discipline and strategic direction. Self-governance addresses the inherent risks of prolonged power and is essential for maintaining its leadership capacity during demanding phases. The implications are significant. Internal regulations, oversight, anti-corruption efforts and cadre evaluation form a Party-building experience worth examining beyond conventional categories used to understand political systems. The ultimate test will be whether the Party can translate internal renewal into better policies, greater administrative effectiveness, improved self-correction and closer alignment with the aspirations of the people. It will also depend on preserving cadre initiative while maintaining accountability and control over the exercise of power. A Party in good working order is not merely a disciplined Party; it learns, corrects itself and mobilizes its members to respond to society's needs. The author is the founder and emeritus adviser of the Observatory of Chinese Politics. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily. item.title: 9th China International Import Expo opens in Shanghai
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
SHANGHAI -- The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE) opened on Thursday in Shanghai. Running from Nov 5 to 10, this year's CIIE has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors, with total exhibition area exceeding 440,000 square meters. Over 480 exhibits are set to make their global, Asian or China debut at the event, the highest number in history.

item.title: US companies' presence at CIIE expands
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Companies from the United States are expanding their presence at China's flagship import expo, underscoring China's enduring appeal as a consumer market and manufacturing hub amid an evolving global trade and investment landscape. From agricultural products and advanced manufacturing technologies, to innovative industrial goods and logistics solutions, US companies including Archer-Daniels-Midland, Rockwell Automation, 3M and FedEx are showcasing their latest offerings at the 9th China International Import Expo, which runs from Thursday to Tuesday in Shanghai. Senior executives from those companies said that China's vast market, industrial upgrading and growing demand for innovation continue to create opportunities for US businesses. US exhibitors have secured more than 50,000 square meters of exhibition space at the CIIE this year, an increase of 1,500 square meters from last year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. The US has ranked first among participating countries and regions by exhibition area for eight consecutive years. ADM, the Chicago, Illinois-based agribusiness group and a seven-time CIIE participant, plans to sign agreements worth 32 billion yuan ($4.8 billion) with customers and industry partners for soybean and grain imports at this year's expo. Quan Ping, president of ADM China, said the CIIE provides an opportunity to better understand customer needs, deepen industry partnerships and turn global expertise into practical solutions tailored to the Chinese market. "We aim to combine our global capabilities with local market insights to create greater value for customers and partners, while bringing more innovative products and solutions to China," Quan said. Rockwell Automation, which is exhibiting at the CIIE for the sixth consecutive year, is showcasing new automation controllers and smart manufacturing solutions as the US company seeks to tap into China's growing demand for industrial artificial intelligence and more efficient production systems. Ian Shih, president of Rockwell Automation (China), said his company sees opportunities in China's intelligent equipment, new energy, life sciences, advanced manufacturing and industrial digitalization sectors, driven by growing demand for smarter and more flexible production systems. Fu Suixin, an associate researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of American Studies, said that US multinationals increasingly see China as more than a sales market, given its role in global innovation and supply chains and the deep economic ties between the two countries. Investment momentum The continued interest is also reflected in investment flows. China's actual use of foreign investment from the US rose 7.7 percent year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, while more than 6,300 foreign-invested companies made additional investments in China, data from the Ministry of Commerce showed. US industrial group 3M, which has never missed an edition of the CIIE, is showcasing its latest technologies and products in automotive, electronics, safety, manufacturing materials and automation, with several products making their global or China debuts. "We have always viewed the CIIE as a key trade fair for showcasing cutting-edge innovations and expanding local partnerships," said Henry Ding, president of 3M China. He added that 3M and Chinese sportswear company Anta Sports Products will sign a memorandum of understanding at the event to establish a joint innovation laboratory focused on applications of sustainable materials in outdoor sports. US express transportation company FedEx is showcasing solutions in smart logistics, sustainable operations and specialized transportation services this year at the CIIE. Poh-Yian Koh, president of FedEx China, said that as AI, digitalization and evolving supply chains reshape global commerce, Chinese businesses need more than transportation. They require trusted partners that can provide the connectivity, visibility and resilience needed to expand globally. Wu Di, deputy head of the department of foreign investment administration at the Ministry of Commerce, said China will expand opening-up trials in cloud computing, biotechnology and wholly foreign-owned hospitals, and create new opportunities in emerging industries and digital and low-carbon development.

item.title: CIIE demonstrates potential of Chinese market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
There is a selective myopia in the way some in the West discuss China, focusing too sharply on its export capabilities while overlooking what the world's second-largest economy imports and the opportunities its vast market offers foreign businesses. As protectionism and unilateralism disrupt the global trading system, the ninth China International Import Expo, opening in Shanghai on Thursday, offers a useful corrective lens for this shortsightedness. Since its inception in 2018 as the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, the CIIE has evolved into an international public good: a platform through which businesses, economies and developing countries can gain access to China's development opportunities. This year's event has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors from 148 countries and regions, including more than 2,000 first-time participants. That is hardly the profile of a market "taking advantage of" others. The persistence of the so-called "China Shock" narrative rests on an inversion. China's manufacturing competitiveness is falsely presented as a "threat", while the benefits of its enormous market, comprehensive industrial ecosystem and growing demand are routinely pushed into the background. The result is a political construct that turns economic interdependence into a zero-sum contest. The facts tell a different story. China's foreign trade in goods reached 39.94 trillion yuan ($5.94 trillion) in the first three quarters of 2026, up 18.8 percent year-on-year. More tellingly, imports grew by 22.3 percent to 16.74 trillion yuan, outpacing the 16.4 percent increase in exports to 23.2 trillion yuan. This is not the typical picture of an economy interested only in selling to the rest of the world. Nor is the story confined to merchandise. China's imports and exports of services rose 8.5 percent to 5.77 trillion yuan during the same period year-on-year. Services exports increased by 14.8 percent to 2.27 trillion yuan, while imports reached 3.5 trillion yuan. The services trade deficit narrowed by 132.66 billion yuan year-on-year. These figures suggest an economy whose international integration is becoming more sophisticated, extending well beyond factories and shipping containers. The CIIE makes these opportunities tangible. For African merchants, participation helps them replace intermediaries with direct relationships with Chinese buyers. German logistics company Jungheinrich now uses its Shanghai manufacturing base to serve 42 countries and regions. That shows access to China can generate business, investment and innovation far beyond China itself. The benefits are not reserved for multinational corporations. This year's expo has increased free exhibition space for least developed countries by 17 percent. China's extension of eligible zero-tariff treatment to goods from 53 African countries also provides a wider framework for developing countries to expand their exports. The broader context matters, too. At the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting on Tuesday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Commerce Minister Wang Wentao called on member economies to uphold free trade, strengthen regional integration and advance cooperation in openness, innovation and sustainable development. More than 300 meetings and events have been successfully held during the APEC "China Year", producing a series of cooperation outcomes. The theme of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in November, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", captures an alternative to the fragmentation now threatening global supply chains. China's pursuit of high-quality development that is innovation-driven, sustainable and inclusive means its industrial upgrading, structural adjustment, domestic demand and high-standard opening-up will continue to create cooperation opportunities and development dividends for other economies. The world has far more to gain from recognizing the "China Opportunity" than from the "China Shock" falsehood that some use to obscure it.

item.title: In search of starry, starry nights
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
When Ge Yixiao stepped out of her car at Ngari Dark Sky Park, the Milky Way stretched across the night sky above her — a sight she had never witnessed before. Ge was on a self-driving trip through Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region in August when viewers of her livestream strongly urged her to visit the park in Ngari prefecture. Their enthusiasm convinced her to make the detour. "The moment I got out of the car, I couldn't stop saying how beautiful it was," she recalled. "I came back again two nights later." Zhou Zhanglong, a keen stargazer, had visited the park the previous year but missed a clear view of the Milky Way because of bad weather. When he returned this year, he placed stargazing high on his itinerary. This time, he captured photos of the Milky Way using time-lapse photography on his phone and shared the images with friends. The two experiences reflect travelers' growing interest in going to places where the stars can still be seen clearly, turning the night sky into a reason to make a journey. Beyond its value to tourism, however, the natural night sky is essential to astronomical research and wildlife, making dark sky protection an issue of environmental conservation as well as development. Across China, efforts to preserve this resource are taking different forms, from the remote, high-altitude plateau of Ngari to the astronomical observation hub of Lenghu in Qinghai province and Xichong on the outskirts of Guangdong province's Shenzhen, one of China's largest cities.

item.title: China's win-win philosophy is an ancient idea
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
An ancient line from Yu Xin of the Southern and Northern Dynasties (420-581) tells us: "When you reap fruits, you remember the tree; when you drink water, you remember its source." China's relations with other countries are not simply about taking what it can get. They involve a process of mutual benefit and reciprocity. This is genuine win-win cooperation, not zero-sum rivalry.
